name: Tethered Orbital Reconnaissance and Suppression Drone TORSD-7 'Kitestring'
description:
The TORSD-7 is a high-altitude tethered drone platform designed for persistent area suppression and overwatch. Unlike free-flight drones, the Kitestring operates on a conductive monofilament tether up to 180 meters in length, anchored to a ground station the size of a briefcase. The tether serves dual purposes: it provides continuous power to the drone, eliminating battery constraints, and it carries the electrothermal discharge rail that is the platform's primary weapon system. The drone maintains a stable hover via four counter-rotating ducted fans and positions itself above a target area while the ground station operator designates firing solutions through a handheld interface.

The weapon system works by charging the tether itself to extreme voltage and then releasing a directed electrothermal burst downward along a secondary projected filament fired from the drone's undercarriage. The projected filament is a ultra-fine conductive thread, weighted and aimed, that drapes across a target or target area. On contact, the ground station completes the circuit and delivers a high-amperage electrothermal pulse through the filament. The effect on unshielded human targets is immediate cardiac and neuromuscular disruption. On vehicles or electronic systems, the pulse induces catastrophic circuit failure.

The TORSD-7's distinctive silhouette — a hovering shape connected to the ground by a nearly invisible thread — has earned it a reputation for surreal, almost supernatural lethality. Victims and witnesses frequently report not understanding how or from where the strike came. Zheng-Dao Bioelectric developed the platform for infrastructure protection contracts in contested industrial zones, but the design was widely copied and the black market variant, the 'Barefoot,' strips the IFF systems and sells the ground station as a portable backpack unit.
tier_availability: Tier 5+ / Military only / Black market (Barefoot variant)
specifications:
tether length: Up to 180 meters
tether material: Tungsten-carbon composite monofilament, 0.3mm diameter
drone dimensions: 62cm rotor span
drone mass: 3.8kg
ground station mass: 4.2kg
operational altitude: 15–180 meters
discharge voltage: 18,000V peak
projected filament range: 22 meters lateral from hover position
recharge cycle: 4.5 seconds between discharges
wind tolerance: Operational up to 45 km/h crosswind
acoustic signature: 61dB at 30 meters
tactical_use: Deployed at the perimeter of a defended position to provide persistent overwatch. The ground station operator can designate targets via thermal or optical feed from the drone's sensor package. The near-invisible tether and filament make target identification of the weapon source extremely difficult — most victims are struck before understanding the threat geometry. Used by defensive teams to hold chokepoints, stairwells, and open plazas. The tether's conductive properties also allow the operator to pulse a low-voltage 'warning' discharge through a dropped filament, though field operators rarely use this setting.
cultural_context: The Kitestring is associated with paranoia and contested space in GLMZ. In neighborhoods where territorial disputes are common, residents have developed the habit of looking up before crossing open areas — a behavior the local press has termed 'wirewalker's reflex.' The drone's silence and the nearly invisible nature of the tether have made it a subject of urban legend, with some communities attributing unexplained deaths to 'the leash' without being able to prove the weapon's presence. Corporate zones that deploy TORSD-7 systems do not advertise the fact, and the drones are painted to match sky conditions.
known_users: High-value corporate site perimeter defense teams
Well-funded territorial gang operations in the outer industrial zones
Black market arms dealers offering the 'Barefoot' variant to mid-tier operators
A known mercenary unit called the Filament Boys, who use the platform as their signature
story_hooks: Three bodies have been found in an open plaza with identical cardiac trauma and no visible entry wounds — the local fixer suspects a Kitestring deployment but needs someone to find the ground station anchor point.
A corporate whistleblower is hiding in a building surrounded by an active TORSD-7 perimeter — the party needs to map the tether geometry before attempting extraction.
Someone is selling Barefoot variant ground stations out of a transit locker network — the components are traced to a Zheng-Dao Bioelectric assembly plant with an inside source.
A street kid found what she thought was a fishing line in an alleyway and pulled it — she's in a burn ward now, and her older brother wants the operator's name.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, insectoid quadcopter suspended by an almost imperceptible thread. The drone's body is compact and angular, with four ducted fan shrouds arranged in an X-pattern. The undercarriage bristles with sensor clusters and a visible filament-projection port. From below, it appears to float in impossible stillness, defying gravity.
physical_description.dimensions: Drone: 62cm rotor span, 18cm fuselage length, 14cm height. Tether: up to 180 meters, 0.3mm diameter (nearly invisible to naked eye). Ground station: 28cm × 22cm × 12cm briefcase form factor.
physical_description.weight_description: The drone feels almost weightless in hover — deliberately engineered for minimal inertia. The ground station is deceptively dense; its 4.2kg mass is concentrated in a compact package designed to be shouldered or mounted to a vehicle hardpoint. The monofilament tether is imperceptible in hand until tension is applied.
physical_description.primary_material: Drone frame: carbon-fiber composite with titanium motor mounts. Ducted fans: reinforced polymer composites. Tether: tungsten-carbon composite monofilament. Ground station chassis: magnesium alloy with embedded power capacitor arrays. Heat-dissipation fins visible on station exterior.
physical_description.finish: Drone body: matte gunmetal gray with slight iridescent sheen from carbon weave. Sensor housings: matte black polymer with faint blue accent lighting around optical arrays. Ducted fans: brushed aluminum with faint scorch marks from electrothermal discharge bleed. Ground station: weathered bare magnesium with oxidation patina, scuffed polymer control surfaces. Tether barely visible unless backlit.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary, matte black accents, faint electric blue indicator rings around sensor clusters. Station uses industrial safety yellow on control edges. Worn natural metal tones where finish is compromised.
physical_description.grip_texture: Ground station control surfaces: rubberized polymer with subtle grip ridges. The handheld interface dial is knurled steel. All touch points are designed for operation with augmented fingers or gloved hands.
distinctive_features: Nearly invisible monofilament tether visible only in strong backlight or when dripping water
Four counter-rotating ducted fans in X-configuration with minimal acoustic signature
Undercarriage filament-projection port — a small triangular aperture with faint carbon scoring
Thermal sensor cluster mounted forward; small red indicator lens
Blue LED pulse indicators on drone body that strobe during charge cycles
Ground station cooling fins dissipating waste heat in visible warping patterns
Wear marks on station from field deployment and cable routing
Faint corona discharge marks visible on tether connection points under magnification
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Zheng-Dao Bioelectric hexagonal logo etched into ground station chassis near power input; serial plate on drone fuselage reads in Hanzi and English; 'TORSD-7' stamped on control interface. Black market Barefoot variants have markings filed or obscured.
physical_description.condition_typical: Military/contract units are immaculately maintained with fresh finishes and tight tolerances. Field-deployed units show carbon scoring from filament discharge, minor warping on station heat sinks, and scuffed control surfaces. Black market Barefoot variants display heavy wear, improvised repairs, corrosion, and crude modifications to tether anchor points.
